sections.h2: How do you contact the Monroe County recording office?
sections.html:
Look for Room 106 of the Administration Building at One Quaker Plaza in Stroudsburg. The main number is 570-517-3969. Doors open at 8:30 in the morning and close at 4:30 in the afternoon on weekdays, with major holidays off.

Walk-in recording and title searches are available, though the county says appointments are strongly encouraged because space is limited. Packages can also arrive by post, or electronically through Simplifile, CSC and EPN. Its record books begin in 1836, the year Monroe County was formed from parts of Northampton and Pike counties, and filings made since August 1995 sit on the Landex system.

Beyond the recording fee itself, the office collects realty transfer tax for the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue and for every municipality and school district in the county. It also collects for the Monroe County Affordable Housing Agency, the Commonwealth Court Computer Automation fund, the Equal Access to Justice program and an archive fund for historical preservation of the land records.

A fax line is also listed, 570-517-3873. The Recorder also runs a free Record Alert System, which sends a notice whenever a document is filed under the subscriber's name. An owner who wants to know about any filing against a property can sign up for it.

sections.h2: What does the Monroe County fee bill charge to file a deed?
sections.html:
A deed or mortgage costs $87.75 under the fee bill that took effect November 17, 2025 and was revised the next day with no fee increase. The bill adds $2.00 for each page over four, $0.50 for each name over four, and $10.00 for each tax code number on a document.

Source: Monroe County Recorder of Deeds fee bill. Realty transfer tax is listed as 1 percent state and 1 percent local.

The bill also sets payment rules. It turns away personal checks, demands the exact amount because the office makes no change and gives no refunds, and adds a $2.00 charge to any document that is rejected. Include a postage-paid return envelope so originals can come back.

sections.h2: What must a Monroe County deed contain before the Recorder will accept it?
sections.html:
The county wants an original that is signed, dated and acknowledged in front of a notary, showing the notary's seal, signature and expiration date. Fees and transfer taxes are all due the moment the deed is presented.

  • A tax code number for the parcel.
  • A property description that names the municipality.
  • Payment of the transfer tax. If the tax is unpaid or the deed does not show true value, as with a $1.00 deed, a Statement of Value goes in as two copies and the county forwards it to the state.
  • A return envelope with postage already on it.

Staff will not draft a deed for anyone. Once recorded, a deed stays as written, so adding a spouse or fixing an error means recording a new deed or a deed of correction. Originals go back to the buyer, and mortgages go to the lender. On the lender side, Act 197 lets a satisfaction piece be recorded without the original mortgage or a certified copy of it.

sections.h2: Who pays transfer tax on a Monroe County sale?
sections.html:
The state share and the municipal share are 1 percent apiece, applied to the property's value, which the county warns can differ from the sale price. Contracts often split the bill between the two sides. Even so, a deed is turned away unless the tax is paid when it is presented, and the new owner carries the risk if the amount is questioned later.

The county FAQ lists the family exemptions as a husband and wife, from parent to child, from grandparent to grandchild, and among brothers and sisters, and it adds deeds between former spouses. Non-profit corporations get no break. State revenue guidance also exempts deeds handed to government units and property that passes by inheritance.

A state investigator can decide that a property was worth more than the value stated, or that a claimed exemption fails. The Department then mails the owner a determination. Extra tax and interest are paid to the state, a matching municipal sum is paid at the recorder's office, and the deed is recorded again for regular fees.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Monroe County property tax?
sections.html:
Delinquent real estate taxes go to the Monroe County Tax Claim Bureau, which handles 20 municipalities and four school districts and receives about 9,000 delinquent returns a year. It was created when Act 542 of 1947, the Pennsylvania Real Estate Tax Sale Law, took effect, with the aim of putting tax-delinquent properties back on the productive rolls.

The bureau is down the hall in Room 104 of the same building, at 570-517-3172, and works weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30. Its page offers a lien certificate, which a seller with overdue taxes should request so the closing agent can see what must come out of the proceeds. Counter payments can be made with a money order, a cashier's check or a card, and repository sales run through Bid4Assets.

Anyone behind on taxes should call the bureau before listing, because the balance has to be settled as part of any sale.

sections.h2: What does the Pocono setting mean for a Monroe County seller?
sections.html:
Stroudsburg is the county seat of this Pocono county in northeast Pennsylvania, which the 2020 census put at 168,327 people. It borders Northampton County and the Lehigh Valley to the south, the Delaware River and New Jersey to the east, and Pike, Wayne, Carbon and Luzerne counties on its other sides. About 608 square miles are land.

The county grew fast in the late twentieth century as New York commuters and Pocono tourism arrived, and the 2020 census listed 79,114 housing units, 21.3 percent of them vacant. About three in four occupied homes (76.6 percent) had an owner living in them.

Public schools run through four districts: East Stroudsburg Area, Pleasant Valley, Pocono Mountain and Stroudsburg Area. Interstates 80 and 380 are the main highways, and East Stroudsburg University anchors the town of the same name. Part of the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area, a park of nearly 70,000 acres, lies inside the county, and the Appalachian Trail runs along its southern edge. The Monroe County Transit Authority, known locally as the Pocono Pony, runs fixed bus routes.

faqs.q: What is the Monroe County deed recording fee?
faqs.a: A deed or mortgage starts at $87.75. The bill adds $2.00 for every page past four, $0.50 for every name past four, and $10.00 for each tax code number on the document.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Monroe County recording fee with a personal check?
faqs.a: No. The fee bill rules out personal checks and requires the exact amount, with no change or refunds. Ask the office which payment forms it takes before sending a package.
Yes. Simplifile, CSC and EPN are the three e-recording routes the county lists, and paper still works by post or at the Stroudsburg counter.

faqs.q: Which Monroe County deeds are exempt from transfer tax?
faqs.a: Family deeds between spouses, down the line from parent or grandparent, or among brothers and sisters are exempt, and so are deeds between ex-spouses. Non-profit corporations are not exempt. For any other case the county advises talking to an attorney.

faqs.q: Who collects overdue Monroe County property tax?
faqs.a: The Tax Claim Bureau, Room 104 at One Quaker Plaza in Stroudsburg. Its counter takes money orders, cashier's checks and cards, and the bureau can issue a lien certificate for a sale.
